newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary CPI may rise after sharp May fall-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Hungary CPI may rise after sharp May fall-analysts.

text.p: Hungary's year-on-year inflation dropped almost one percentage point in May but analysts said on Wednesday it could rise again temporarily over the next three months.

"For the three months beginning with June we forecast rising inflation," said GKI Reserach Institute's Judit Barta, adding that it could go up to 19 percent in August but would fall back by the end on the year."

The Central Statistical office said earlier on Wednesday that the consumer price index (CPI) was 1.3 percent up in May month-on-month and showed a 17.7 percent year-on-year rise, compared with April's respective 1.4 and 18.6 percent increases.
Analysts said the slowdown in year-on-year inflation was due to relatively high price levels in May 1996.

"Mathematically (the slowdown) was not a surprise," said Peter Duronelly of Budapest Investment Fund Management Rt. "The month-on-month rise was as high as 2.1 percent in May 1996 because March energy price increases appeared on bills then."
Analysts added that the next quarter year was likely to end the trend of the last 16 months when year-on-year inflation either fell or was steady for every month.
They said the CPI was likely to be stagnant or to rise in July and August, adding that comparative month-on-month CPI rises were little last summer.
"The month-on-month indices were very low last summer," said Zoltan Bereczki of New York Broker.
Barta added that fruit and vegetable prices even dropped one year ago.
"Looking at the current prices, they are not likely to repeat that," she said.

Bereczki said the drop in inflation in May was likely to encourage the government and the central bank to cut the monthly 1.1 percent devaluation rate of the forint by some 10 basis points for the second half of the year.
"I can imagine that a cut in the devaluation rate will be announced within a few weeks," he said.
Other analysts also said before the publication of the May CPI figures that a reduction of about 10 basis points was likely.

Analysts said that inflation is likely to continue to fall from September, although some of them added that November and mainly December would bring a rise again due to low comparative figures at the end of 1996.
Hungary's inflation target for December is 16 to 17 percent.
The forecasts of 13 analysts in a recent Reuters survey ranged between 16 and 19.2 percent.
